summary.headline: Black Box Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA rose 38% to INR160 crore; FY27 revenue guided at INR7,800-8,000 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR1,719 crore (+24% YoY), with EBITDA of INR160 crore (+38% YoY, margin 9.3%, up 90 bps) and PAT of INR56 crore (+18% YoY). The quarter included about two months of consolidation from the Brazilian acquisition 2S, which contributed about INR60 crore. Order bookings were US$339 million and the order backlog reached about US$950 million (up 83% since the transformation began). Management reiterated FY27 guidance, with FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9.3-9.4%, and said growth would be weighted to H2 and spill into FY28.

financial_highlights.change: up 83% since start of transformation; company said up 83% YoY in opening remarks

segments.name: Hyperscale / data center
segments.commentary: Management expects hyperscale to grow about 25% in aggregate across the business, with data center tenures of 24-36 months. A new US hyperscaler order of US$131 million (about INR1,240 crore) was added, with work on site starting from November.

segments.name: Non-hyperscale enterprise
segments.commentary: Expected to grow at modest double-digit, about 10%, lagging the hyperscale cycle, with enterprise spend expected to follow with a lag.

segments.name: Product business (TPS / KVM, Emerald)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making at EBIT level as revenue grows; management expects about 20% growth in FY27 and says the segment is highly accretive once scale is reached.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA INR725-750 crore (+27-32% YoY); EBITDA margin 9.3-9.4% (about +30-40 bps). Medium-term aim is 10% or more at scale.

FY27 order bookings US$1.3-1.4 billion (about +32-45% YoY); order backlog at March 31, 2027 of US$1.3-1.4 billion (about +65-75%). Management said the backlog figure may be conservative and gave updated detail after Q2.
Tax rate expected at 10-15% in FY27 and FY28, normalising to about 20% thereafter.
Operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion expected to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Long-term aspiration of INR18,000 crore (US$2 billion) revenue by FY30: about INR12,000 crore organic and INR6,000 crore inorganic.
capex_capacity: Plan to onboard nearly 2,000 professionals to support execution.
Large hyperscale sites are gigawatt-plus; deployment and hiring for the new US hyperscaler order start only from November.
Talent and people investment described as largely done; cash flow expected to turn positive from operations.
Management said supply chain, particularly cables and fibre, improved over the last quarter.
demand_pricing: Management says competition is based on execution capability, scale, and the ability to deploy skilled resources, not on lowest price.
Management estimates the addressable opportunity at US$250-300 billion, with about 60-70% of spending in the US.
Management says the company has executed several hundred megawatts, close to a gigawatt, and is now receiving more invitations to bid (pull rather than push).
Data center orders are described as accretive to margin, and expected to be more accretive at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What was organic revenue growth given 2S was included from May?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said INR60 crore of the INR1,719 crore came from 2S, and the balance is organic. June quarter is seasonally weak for 2S.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow improve given the investment needs suggested by the backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said talent investment is largely complete, operating cash flow should be positive, and cash flow should rise with growth. Working capital still needs funding.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative, given backlog growth ex-long-term projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said most backlog execution falls in Q3 and Q4, and it will spill into FY28. FY27 growth is about 22-25% and FY28 growth should exceed that. Backlog could end higher as new orders come in Oct-Mar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for non-data center businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said non-hyperscale enterprise is expected to grow about 10%, with a lag behind the hyperscale cycle. Overall growth is about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will TPS / product business reach profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the product business is expected to grow about 20% in FY27 and focus on mission-critical products such as KVM/Emerald. Losses should narrow with scale.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance imply depressed Q2/Q3 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said Q4 should be at or above 10%. Investment in training and talent means guidance is kept at 9.3-9.4% for the year, with 10% or more expected at scale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from hyperscaler capex moderation?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said current pipeline shows new projects being announced and no slowdown in conversations. Shifts between sites would be absorbed across multiple geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive moat?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO cited scale, execution capability, customer relationships, and the ability to fund and train staff. He said competition will exist, and the company is aiming to take share.

risks_watch: Guidance depends on H2 conversion: Q1 was described as seasonally soft, and FY27 growth requires about 30-40% sequential or YoY growth in H2.
Margin: management is holding guidance at 9.3-9.4% because of talent and training investment, and 10% is targeted only at scale.
Customer concentration in hyperscalers: any capex moderation or site delay would affect execution and backlog timing.
Product business (TPS) still loss-making at EBIT level.
Working capital and cash conversion needs to improve meaningfully over FY26.
Tax rate is currently low due to carried-forward losses; it is expected to rise to about 20% after FY28.
Transcript notes that several guidance figures were corrected on the call (backlog, bookings, EBITDA, PAT, margin); use the corrected figures stated in the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on demand and backlog, with explicit caution on margins (guidance held at 9.3-9.4% because of investment in talent) and on H2 execution timing. Management relied on the backlog to support the FY27 numbers and gave limited detail on cash flow and on the product business.
